title.en: Israel and Lebanon agree to extend ceasefire, US state department says
title.zh: 美国国务院称以色列和黎巴嫩同意延长停火

summary.en: The US State Department announced an agreement between Israel and Lebanon to extend a ceasefire. This truce was initially declared by President Trump last month, but reports indicate that Israel and Hezbollah have continued to engage in exchanges of fire since its inception.
summary.zh: 美国国务院宣布以色列和黎巴嫩同意延长停火。这项停火协议最初由特朗普总统于上月宣布，但有报道称，自协议生效以来，以色列和真主党之间仍持续交火。

body.en:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed a 45-day extension to a shaky ceasefire, following two days of negotiations in Washington DC, the US state department said.

"We hope these discussions will advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and establishing genuine security along their shared border," said state department spokesman Tommy Pigott.

US President Donald Trump announced the truce on 16 April, but Israel and Hezbollah have continued to exchange fire since then.

On Wednesday, Lebanon's health ministry said Israeli air strikes had killed 22 people, including eight children, across the south.

The state department said it would "reconvene the political track of negotiations" in June.

"In addition, a security track will be launched at the Pentagon on May 29 with military delegations from both countries," Pigott added.

Israel's Ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, said the talks were "frank and constructive".

Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said that he hoped to "mobilise all Arab and international support to bolster our position in the negotiations" with Israel.

There have been almost daily reports of Hezbollah and Israel trading fire across the southern border of Lebanon since the ceasefire began.

Israel has intensified its air and artillery strikes in recent days, particularly in southern Lebanon, saying it was targeting Hezbollah fighters and infrastructure.

Lebanon's health ministry has accused Israel of targeting civilians and paramedics, which Israel denies.

The Israeli military says it is aiming to create a buffer zone in southern Lebanon to thwart future Hezbollah attacks.

In those areas, entire villages have been destroyed in similar tactics deployed by the Israeli military in Gaza. Human rights groups say some cases could amount to war crimes, which Israel denies.

Hezbollah has carried out its own attacks on Israeli troops in Lebanon and northern Israel with rockets and drones.

Southern Lebanon is the heartland of the country's Shia community, from which Hezbollah gets most of its support, and has been under constant Israeli bombardment.

More than one million people, amounting to one in five of the population, have been forced from their homes across Lebanon, most of them from the south, the eastern Bekaa Valley, and the southern suburbs of Beirut known as Dahieh, areas where Hezbollah holds sway.

The conflict started on 2 March, two days after the US and Israel launched a joint attack on Iran.

Hezbollah fired rockets into Israel, and Israel responded with widespread air strikes and a ground invasion of southern Lebanon.

At least 2,896 people have been killed in Lebanon since then, according to the health ministry.

body.zh: 美国国务院表示，经过两天在华盛顿特区的谈判，以色列和黎巴嫩已同意将不稳定的停火期限延长 45 天。 美国国务院发言人汤米·皮戈特表示：“我们希望这些讨论将促进两国之间的持久和平，充分承认彼此的主权和领土完整，并在两国共同边界建立真正的安全。” 美国总统特朗普于4月16日宣布停战，但以色列和真主党此后持续交火。 周三，黎巴嫩卫生部表示，以色列的空袭已造成南部地区 22 人死亡，其中包括 8 名儿童。 美国国务院表示将在六月“重新启动谈判的政治轨道”。 皮戈特补充说：“此外，五角大楼将于 5 月 29 日与两国军事代表团一起启动安全轨道。” 自停火开始以来，几乎每天都有报道称真主党和以色列在黎巴嫩南部边境交火。 以色列最近几天加强了空袭和炮击，特别是在黎巴嫩南部，称其目标是真主党战士和基础设施。 黎巴嫩卫生部指责以色列针对平民和护理人员，但以色列对此予以否认。 以色列军方表示，其目标是在黎巴嫩南部建立一个缓冲区，以阻止真主党未来的袭击。 在这些地区，以色列军队在加沙采取的类似策略摧毁了整个村庄。人权组织表示，有些案件可能构成战争罪，但以色列否认了这一点。 真主党也用火箭和无人机对黎巴嫩和以色列北部的以色列军队发动了袭击。 冲突始于3月2日，即美国和以色列对伊朗发动联合攻击两天后。 真主党向以色列发射火箭，以色列则以大范围的空袭和对黎巴嫩南部的地面入侵作为回应。 据黎巴嫩卫生部称，自那时以来，黎巴嫩已有至少 2,896 人死亡。 以色列当局称，同期有 18 名士兵和 4 名平民被杀。

reflection.en: Even as leaders work to extend ceasefires, the ongoing exchange of fire reminds us how challenging true peace can be. Romans 12:18 calls us to live at peace with everyone, "if it is possible, as far as it depends on you." This verse acknowledges the human effort required to move from truce to lasting tranquility, even when obstacles remain.
reflection.zh: 即使领导人努力延长停火，持续的交火也提醒我们真正的和平是多么具有挑战性。罗马书12:18呼吁我们“若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦”。这节经文承认，即使障碍依然存在，从休战走向持久的安宁也需要人类的努力。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Judge declares another mistrial in Harvey Weinstein New York rape case
title.zh: 法官宣布哈维·韦恩斯坦纽约强奸案再次流审

summary.en: A New York judge declared a mistrial in the rape case against former film mogul Harvey Weinstein, marking the third time a jury has deliberated on the charges without reaching a verdict.
summary.zh: 纽约一名法官宣布，针对前电影大亨哈维·韦恩斯坦的强奸案再次流审，这是纽约陪审团第三次审议此案而未能达成裁决。

body.en:
A judge has declared a mistrial in the rape case against Harvey Weinstein, after the jury in New York said it was deadlocked and unable to reach a verdict.

It marks the third time a New York jury has considered the case against the 74-year-old disgraced film mogul, who remains jailed on other charges.

The month-long trial was centred around whether Weinstein raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann in a hotel room more than a decade ago. He was initially convicted of raping her, before the verdict was overturned. A judge declared a mistrial after a second trial last year.

Dozens of women have come forward with allegations of sexual misconduct, including rape, against Weinstein since October 2017. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.

Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said in a statement that prosecutors are currently determining whether to try again in court.

"While we are disappointed that the proceedings ended with a mistrial, we deeply respect the jury system and sincerely thank all of the jurors for their time and dedication," he said.

He thanked Mann for bringing her allegation against Weinstein, adding: "We will consider our next steps in consultation with Ms Mann, and in consideration of Harvey Weinstein's pending sentencing" in a separate sexual assault case.

"As always, we will continue to prosecute crimes of sexual violence – no matter who the defendant is – in a survivor-centered manner that uplifts their voices in the pursuit of justice."

Lawyers for Weinstein said the outcome shows "how deeply public perception and prejudice surrounding Harvey Weinstein have become embedded in society".

"For some people, regardless of the evidence presented, saying 'not guilty' has become emotionally or socially impossible," they argued.

"The Manhattan District Attorney's Office should stop retrying the same case and focus its time and resources on the actual violent crime, chaos, and public safety issues impacting New Yorkers every day," the statement from his lawyers continued.

The decision on Friday by the majority-male jury in Manhattan came on the third day of deliberations.

On Friday morning, the jury passed the judge a note saying they "have concluded that they cannot reach" a unanimous verdict. The judge then ordered them to continue deliberating before later declaring a mistrial, saying it was "quite clear," that they were "hopelessly deadlocked".

"I see no reason to go any further," said Judge Curtis Farber as he thanked and dismissed the jury.

Weinstein, who was seated in a wheelchair during the trial, showed no facial expression as court officers wheeled him out of the room after the mistrial was declared.

body.zh: 纽约陪审团称案件陷入僵局无法做出裁决后，一名法官宣布哈维·韦恩斯坦强奸案审判无效。 这是纽约陪审团第三次审议针对这位名誉扫地的 74 岁电影大亨的案件，他目前仍因其他指控而入狱。 为期一个月的审判围绕韦恩斯坦是否十多年前在酒店房间强奸了有抱负的女演员杰西卡·曼恩。他最初被判强奸她，但后来判决被推翻。去年二审后，一名法官宣布审判无效。 自 2017 年 10 月以来，已有数十名女性站出来指控温斯坦有不当性行为，包括强奸。他一直否认有不当行为。 曼哈顿地区检察官阿尔文·布拉格在一份声明中表示，检察官目前正在决定是否在法庭上再次审理。 他说：“虽然我们对诉讼程序以误审结束感到失望，但我们深深尊重陪审团制度，并真诚感谢所有陪审员的时间和奉献精神。” 他感谢曼对韦恩斯坦提出指控，并补充道：“我们将与曼女士协商，并考虑哈维·韦恩斯坦在另一起性侵犯案件中的未决判决，考虑下一步的行动。” “一如既往，我们将继续以以幸存者为中心的方式起诉性暴力犯罪，无论被告是谁，提高他们追求正义的声音。” 韦恩斯坦的律师表示，这一结果表明“公众对哈维·韦恩斯坦的看法和偏见已经深入社会”。 “对于一些人来说，无论提供什么证据，说‘无罪’在情感上或社交上都是不可能的，”他们辩称。 他的律师在声明中继续说道：“曼哈顿地区检察官办公室应该停止重审同一案件，并将时间和资源集中在每天影响纽约人的实际暴力犯罪、混乱和公共安全问题上。” 曼哈顿由男性占多数的陪审团在审议的第三天做出了周五的决定。 周五早上，陪审团向法官传递了一份纸条，称他们“得出结论，无法达成”一致裁决。法官随后命令他们继续审议，随后宣布审判无效，并表示“很明显”，他们“陷入了无可救药的僵局”。 “我认为没有理由再进一步，”柯蒂斯·法伯法官在感谢陪审团并解散时说道。 审判期间坐在轮椅上的韦恩斯坦在宣布无效审判后，法庭工作人员将他推出房间，他没有任何面部表情。 一名陪审员在法庭外对记者表示，陪审团中有九人希望宣判韦恩斯坦无罪，而……

reflection.en: The repeated mistrial in a high-profile case can leave many questioning the effectiveness of the justice system. When legal processes falter, it can feel as though justice is paralyzed, leaving a sense of frustration and unresolved questions. Yet, the pursuit of truth and accountability remains a vital human endeavor, even when the path is long and arduous.
reflection.zh: 一宗备受瞩目案件的反复流审，可能让许多人对司法系统的效力产生疑问。当法律程序受阻时，人们会感到正义似乎陷入停滞，留下沮丧和悬而未决的问题。然而，即使道路漫长而艰辛，对真相和问责的追求仍然是一项至关重要的人类努力。

verse.textEn: The law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verse.textZh: 因此律法放松，公理也不显明；恶人围困义人，所以公理显然颠倒。

summary.en: Israel and Lebanon have agreed to extend their ceasefire by 45 days following talks in Washington, as announced by the US state department. This development occurred amidst ongoing Israeli strikes on the southern city of Tyre.

body.en: Statement following ‘productive’ talks in Washington comes as Israel launches strikes on southern city of Tyre Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 45-day extension of their ceasefire after another round of talks in Washington, the US state department has said. title.en: How team Burnham finally cleared the first of many hurdles on route to Westminster
title.zh: 伯纳姆团队如何最终扫清通往威斯敏斯特的诸多障碍中的第一个

body.en: At one stage the northern mayor looked to be locked out of parliament, again, but he is still only one step along the road to his No 10 ambitions For weeks, Andy Burnham’s supporters had told MPs to “hold the line”, that he had a seat in parliament in his sights and that he would be a contender in any leadership contest. Two leadership contests, a block on a return in Gorton and Denton, and quite a few aggrieved MPs in the north west who have had to spend weeks batting off suggestions they will give their seats up for him. reflection.en: The political journey to high office is often marked by many hurdles and a long road, as seen in this story. While human effort and strategic planning are vital, this path ultimately reminds us that true exaltation and the power to lift up or bring down leaders rest with 雅伟.
reflection.zh: 政治人物通往高位的道路，正如这则新闻所示，往往充满重重障碍且漫长。虽然人的努力和策略性规划至关重要，但这条道路最终提醒我们，真正的提升以及升降掌权者的权柄，都掌握在雅伟手中。

title.en: US to seek death penalty for suspect in killing of Israeli embassy staff members
title.zh: 美国将寻求对杀害以色列使馆工作人员嫌犯判处死刑

summary.en: US government officials allege that Elias Rodriguez shot and killed a young Jewish couple at an event in Washington last May, and are now seeking the death penalty for the suspect.
summary.zh: 美国政府指控埃利亚斯·罗德里格斯于去年五月在华盛顿的一次活动中枪杀了一对年轻的犹太夫妇，目前正寻求对该嫌犯判处死刑。

body.en:
The US government is seeking the death penalty for the suspect charged with killing two Israeli embassy staff members in Washington DC last year.

The US Attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, on Friday filed a notice of intent to seek capital punishment for three out of 13 total charges against 31-year-old Elias Rodriguez. President Donald Trump has embraced the federal death penalty after his predecessor Joe Biden limited its use.

Prosecutors allege Rodriguez opened fire on the couple - Yaron Lischinsky, 30, and Sarah Lynn Milgrim, 26 - outside the Capital Jewish Museum before shouting "Free Palestine" during his arrest in May 2025.

Pirro's office will seek death if Rodriguez is found guilty of the charges of murder of a foreign official, discharge of a firearm during a crime of violence, and causing death through the use of a firearm.

The suspect has also been charged with other offences including hate crimes and acts of terrorism.

"My office will not rest in our efforts to hold Elias Rodriguez accountable for this horrific, and targeted act of terror against Yaron Lischinsky, Sarah Milgrim and our Jewish community," Pirro said earlier this year.

Prosecutors allege that ahead of the shooting, Rodriguez expressed support for violence against Israelis, including in social media posts where he allegedly wrote "Death to Israel".

Prosecutors have said he travelled from Chicago to Washington DC with a handgun after researching an upcoming networking event for young Jewish professionals at the museum.

Lischinsky and Milgrim were leaving when the suspect fired 20 shots, killing them both, prosecutors allege. They were in a relationship and Lischinsky had bought an engagement ring, planning to propose to Milgrim on an upcoming trip to Israel, Israel's ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, previously said.

After the shooting, Rodriguez then allegedly entered the museum, displayed a red keffiyeh, and said: "I did it for Palestine. I did it for Gaza."

Prosecutors also say Rodriguez wrote a document called "explication" in which he expressed his support for Palestine and claimed Israel was trying to exterminate Palestinians.

"In addition to allegedly murdering two innocent people and terrorizing the survivors of his attack at the Capital Jewish Museum, Rodriguez wrote and published a manifesto attempting to morally justify his actions and inspire others to commit political violence," Darren Cox, FBI Assistant Director in Charge of the Washington Field Office, said in a February press release.

body.zh: 美国政府正在寻求对被控去年在华盛顿特区杀害两名以色列大使馆工作人员的嫌疑人判处死刑。 美国哥伦比亚特区检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 周五提交了一份意向通知，拟对 31 岁的埃利亚斯·罗德里格斯 (Elias Rodriguez) 提出的 13 项指控中的 3 项寻求死刑。在他的前任乔·拜登限制死刑的使用后，唐纳德·特朗普总统接受了联邦死刑。 检察官称，罗德里格斯在 2025 年 5 月被捕期间，在首都犹太博物馆外向这对夫妇（30 岁的亚伦·利钦斯基 (Yaron Lischinsky) 和 26 岁的莎拉·林恩·米尔格里姆 (Sarah Lynn Milgrim)）开枪，然后高喊“自由巴勒斯坦”。 如果罗德里格斯被判犯有谋杀外国官员、在暴力犯罪中开枪以及使用枪支致人死亡等罪名，皮罗的办公室将寻求死刑。 嫌疑人还被指控犯有其他罪行，包括仇恨犯罪和恐怖主义行为。 皮罗今年早些时候表示：“我的办公室将不遗余力地追究埃利亚斯·罗德里格斯对亚龙·利辛斯基、莎拉·米尔格里姆和我们犹太社区的这一可怕的、有针对性的恐怖行为的责任。” 检察官称，在枪击事件发生前，罗德里格斯表达了对针对以色列人的暴力的支持，包括在社交媒体帖子中据称他写道“以色列去死”。 检察官表示，他在研究博物馆即将举行的年轻犹太专业人士社交活动后，带着手枪从芝加哥前往华盛顿特区。 检察官称，利辛斯基和米尔格里姆正要离开时，嫌疑人开了 20 枪，两人双双死亡。以色列驻美国大使叶切尔·莱特此前表示，他们正在恋爱，利辛斯基买了一枚订婚戒指，计划在即将前往以色列的旅行中向米尔格里姆求婚。 枪击事件发生后，据称罗德里格斯进入博物馆，展示了红色头巾，并说：“我为巴勒斯坦这样做。我为加沙这样做。” 检察官还称，罗德里格斯撰写了一份名为“解释”的文件，其中表达了对巴勒斯坦的支持，并声称以色列试图消灭巴勒斯坦人。 “除了涉嫌谋杀两名无辜者并恐吓首都犹太博物馆袭击事件的幸存者外，罗德里格斯还撰写并发表了一份宣言，试图在道义上为自己的行为辩护，并煽动其他人实施政治暴力，”负责华盛顿外地办事处的联邦调查局助理局长达伦·考克斯(Darren Cox)在二月份的新闻稿中表示。 特朗普在第一任期内恢复了十多年来未执行过的联邦死刑，并改变了司法政策，使拜登政府随后撤销的死刑更容易执行。拜登随后...

title.en: New outbreak of Ebola kills 65 in eastern DR Congo
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国东部新一轮埃博拉疫情造成 65 人死亡

summary.en: Africa's top health agency says around 246 cases have been reported.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Africa's top health agency has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's eastern Ituri province.

Around 246 cases and 65 deaths have been reported, mainly in the gold-mining towns of Mongwalu and Rwampara, said the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

Ugandan officials confirmed one case of imported Ebola from DR Congo on Friday, with the country's health ministry stating that a 59-year-old male who died on Thursday had tested positive.

Ebola was first discovered in 1976 in what is now DR Congo, and is thought to have spread from bats. This is the 17th outbreak of the deadly viral disease in the country.

It is spread through direct contact with bodily fluids and through broken skin, causing severe bleeding and organ failure.

Early symptoms include fever, muscle pain, fatigue, headache and sore throat, and are followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, a rash and bleeding.

There is no proven cure for Ebola. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the average fatality rate is around 50%.

Preliminary tests conducted at the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) in the capital, Kinshasa, have detected the virus in 13 of 20 samples analysed, following consultations with DR Congo's Ministry of Health and National Public Institute.

Of the 65 deaths, four were reported among lab-confirmed cases, Africa CDC said.

Additional suspected cases have also been reported in Ituri's provincial capital, Bunia, with laboratory confirmation pending.

Africa CDC said it was concerned by the high risk of further spread due to the urban settings of Rwampara and Bunia, and mining activities in Mongwalu.

The health agency's executive director Dr Jean Kaseya added that "significant population movement" between the affected areas and neighbouring countries also meant regional co-ordination was essential.

All affected communities and at-risk areas have been advised to follow guidelines from the national health authorities.

The Congolese government has not yet officially declared an outbreak. A staffer told the BBC a press conference was expected later on Friday.

Its statement on Friday added that it was convening a meeting with DR Congo, neighbouring Uganda and South Sudan, and other international partners to discuss priorities, including response efforts and cross-border surveillance.

Ituri has been under military rule since 2021, with the civilian authority replaced by a military general in an attempt to neutralise dozens of armed groups which have operated in the area for many years. These include the Allied Democratic Forced (ADF), affiliated to the Islamic State group.

On Friday, the Ugandan health department confirmed that an imported case of Ebola had been found, according to a letter shared by...
body.zh: 非洲最高卫生机构宣布刚果民主共和国东部伊图里省爆发埃博拉疫情。 非洲疾病控制和预防中心 (Africa CDC) 表示，已报告约 246 例病例和 65 例死亡，主要发生在金矿城镇蒙瓦卢 (Mongwalu) 和鲁万帕拉 (Rwampara)。 乌干达官员周五确认了一例从刚果民主共和国输入的埃博拉病例，该国卫生部表示，周四死亡的一名 59 岁男性检测结果呈阳性。 埃博拉病毒于 1976 年在现在的刚果民主共和国首次发现，被认为是通过蝙蝠传播的。这是该国第 17 次爆发致命病毒性疾病。 它通过直接接触体液和破损的皮肤传播，导致严重出血和器官衰竭。 早期症状包括发烧、肌肉疼痛、疲劳、头痛和喉咙痛，随后出现呕吐、腹泻、皮疹和出血。 埃博拉病毒尚无有效治疗方法。根据世界卫生组织 (WHO) 的数据，平均死亡率约为 50%。 在与刚果民主共和国卫生部和国家公共研究所协商后，首都金沙萨国家生物医学研究所 (INRB) 进行的初步测试已在分析的 20 个样本中的 13 个样本中检测到了该病毒。 非洲疾病预防控制中心表示，在 65 例死亡中，有 4 例是实验室确诊病例。 伊图里省首府布尼亚还报告了更多疑似病例，有待实验室确认。 非洲疾病预防控制中心表示，由于鲁万帕拉和布尼亚的城市环境以及蒙瓦鲁的采矿活动，该病毒进一步传播的高风险感到担忧。 该卫生机构执行主任让·卡塞亚博士补充说，受影响地区和邻国之间的“大量人口流动”也意味着区域协调至关重要。 建议所有受影响的社区和高危地区遵循国家卫生当局的指导方针。 刚果政府尚未正式宣布疫情爆发。一名工作人员告诉英国广播公司，预计周五晚些时候将举行新闻发布会。 该组织周五的声明补充说，它正在与刚果民主共和国、邻国乌干达和南苏丹以及其他国际伙伴召开会议，讨论优先事项，包括应对工作和跨境监视。 伊图里自 2021 年以来一直处于军事统治之下，文职当局被一名军事将领取代，试图消灭在该地区活动多年的数十个武装团体。其中包括附属于伊斯兰国组织的民主同盟军（ADF）。 根据分享的一封信，周五，乌干达卫生部门确认发现了一例输入性埃博拉病例。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.

title.en: Trump warns Taiwan against declaring independence, hours after summit with China's Xi
title.zh: 与中国习近平峰会数小时后，特朗普警告台湾不要宣布独立

summary.en: The US president says he wants Beijing and Taipei to "cool down" tensions over the self-governing island.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump has cautioned Taiwan against formally declaring independence from China.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent," the US president told Fox News on Friday, at the end of his two-day summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Trump earlier said he had "made no commitment either way" about the self-governing island - which China claims as part of its territory and has not ruled out taking by force.

The US has long supported Taiwan, including being bound by law to provide it with a means of self-defence, but has frequently had to square this alliance with maintaining a diplomatic relationship with China.

Washington's established position is that it does not support Taiwanese independence, with continued ties with Beijing being contingent on its acceptance that there is only one Chinese government.

Many Taiwanese consider themselves to be part of a separate nation - though most are in favour of maintaining the status quo in which Taiwan neither declares independence from China nor unites with it.

In his interview with Fox News, Trump reiterated that US policy on the matter had not changed.

"You know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles (15,289km) to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down."

On the flight back to Washington, the US president had told reporters that he and Xi had spoken "a lot" about the island, but said he had declined to discuss whether the US would defend it.

Xi "feels very strongly" about the island and "doesn't want to see a movement for independence", Trump said.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations," Xi warned during the talks, according to Chinese state media, adding: "If mishandled, the two nations could collide or even come into conflict."

Asked if he foresaw a conflict with China over Taiwan, Trump had said: "No, I don't think so. I think we'll be fine. [Xi] doesn't want to see a war."

China has ramped up military drills around the island in recent years, raising tensions in the region and testing the balance that Washington has struck.

Late last year, the Trump administration announced an $11bn ($8bn) package of weapons to be sold to Taiwan , including advanced rocket launchers and a variety of missiles, which Beijing condemned.

Trump said he would soon decide whether that sale could go ahead, adding that he and Xi had discussed it "in great detail" and that he would speak to Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te first.

"We're not looking to have wars, and if you kept it the way it is, I think China's going to be OK with that. But we're not looking to have somebody say, 'Let's go independent because the United States is backing us'."

The US has previously provoked anger from China for seeming...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普警告台湾不要正式宣布从中国独立。 “我不希望有人独立，”美国总统周五在北京与中国国家主席习近平为期两天的峰会结束时告诉福克斯新闻。 特朗普早些时候表示，他对这个自治岛屿“没有做出任何承诺”——中国声称该岛是其领土的一部分，并且不排除以武力夺取该岛的可能性。 美国长期以来一直支持台湾，包括受法律约束为其提供自卫手段，但经常不得不将这一联盟与维持与中国的外交关系结合起来。 华盛顿的既定立场是，它不支持台湾独立，与北京继续保持关系取决于它是否接受只有一个中国政府。 许多台湾人认为自己是一个独立国家的一部分，尽管大多数人赞成维持现状，即台湾既不宣布从中国独立，也不与中国统一。 特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时重申，美国在此事上的政策没有改变。 “你知道，我们应该行驶 9,500 英里（15,289 公里）去打一场战争。我不是在寻找那个。我希望他们冷静下来。我希望中国冷静下来。” 在返回华盛顿的航班上，美国总统告诉记者，他和习近平就该岛“谈了很多”，但表示他拒绝讨论美国是否会保卫该岛。 特朗普表示，习近平对该岛“感情非常强烈”，并且“不希望看到独立运动”。 据中国官方媒体报道，习近平在会谈中警告称，“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题”，并补充说：“如果处理不当，两国可能发生冲突甚至冲突。” 当被问及是否预见到与中国在台湾问题上发生冲突时，特朗普表示：“不，我不这么认为。我认为我们会没事的。[习近平]不想看到战争。” 近年来，中国加大了在该岛周围的军事演习力度，加剧了该地区的紧张局势，并考验着华盛顿所达成的平衡。 去年年底，特朗普政府宣布向台湾出售价值 110 亿美元（约合 80 亿美元）的一揽子武器，其中包括先进火箭发射器和各种导弹，北京对此予以谴责。 特朗普表示，他将很快决定是否继续进行这项出售，并补充说，他和习近平已经“非常详细”地讨论了此事，他将首先与台湾总统赖清德通话。 “我们不希望发生战争，如果保持现状，我认为中国会对此表示同意。但我们不希望有人说，‘让我们独立吧，因为美国支持我们’。” 此前，美国因看似...而激怒了中国。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Islamic feminism more widespread in Bosnia and Herzegovina
title.zh: 伊斯兰女权主义在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那更加普遍

summary.en: Many Bosnian Muslim women want to attend mosque on Fridays and to play a greater role in decision-making. Slowly the official structures of the Islamic Community are changing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Many Bosnian Muslim women want to attend mosque on Fridays and to play a greater role in decision-making. Slowly the official structures of the Islamic Community are changing.

Usually, it tends to be Muslim men who go to pray on Fridays in the mosques of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As is customary in  Islam , women are not required to go to the mosque to pray on the holiest day of the week. However, more and more, devout Muslim women in the Western Balkan country want to attend the mosque, too.

In the secular state of Bosnia and Herzegovina , men and women are equal before the law. In recent decades, the state has made significant efforts to eliminate gender-based discrimination and protect women from violence. However, in certain religious communities, whether these are Muslim, Orthodox or Catholic , social and cultural norms continue to stand in the way of equality.

Since the end of the Bosnian War (1992–1995), religion has played a greater role in all of the country's communities, particularly amid Muslim Bosniaks, Orthodox Serbs and Catholic Croats. In some families, very conservative notions of gender roles prevail, according to which women are expected first and foremost to be mothers and to care for the family.

"Muslim feminists are fighting for women's rights within an Islamic framework," Bosnian sociologist Dermana Kuric from the University of Sarajevo told DW. She said that they were doing this by taking an active role in society without openly challenging misogynistic interpretations of the Quran.

She added that university educated Muslim women were consciously engaging with traditional Islamic scholarship, which has sought to confine women to a subordinate role in the family and the wider community. "Muslim feminists are concerned with gender relations based on autonomy and individual responsibility — as opposed to control or dominance," Kuric said.

Bosnian Muslim feminists are part of a broader movement that has been gaining influence in the Islamic world since the 1980s. They interpret the Quran from a female perspective and see it as a source of empowerment in their struggle for greater rights. With her translation of the groundbreaking book by Moroccan sociologist and pioneer of Islamic feminism Fatima Mernissi (1940 – 2015) "The Forgotten Queens of Islam," gender studies scholar Zilka Spahic-Siljak from the University of Sarajevo has made a significant contribution to raising awareness of the ideas of Islamic feminism in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

summary.en: At talks in Moldova, more than 30 countries have said they will join a future special tribunal for Ukraine prosecuting Russia over its invasion. How the body will force Russians to stand trial is not clear.

body.zh: 在摩尔多瓦举行的会谈中，30多个国家表示，他们将加入未来的乌克兰特别法庭，起诉俄罗斯的入侵。目前还不清楚该机构将如何迫使俄罗斯人接受审判。 周五，34个欧洲国家加上澳大利亚、哥斯达黎加和欧盟作为一个实体签署了一个未来的特别法庭，该法庭将寻求起诉俄罗斯在入侵乌克兰期间犯下的罪行。 该计划自 2022 年俄罗斯全面入侵后不久就开始酝酿，乌克兰总统泽连斯基去年与欧洲委员会签署了一项协议，寻求实施该计划。 欧洲委员会在一份声明中表示，欧洲委员会的 46 个成员国中的大多数批准了一项决议，为未来的法庭奠定了基础。欧洲委员会是一个总部位于法国的机构，致力于维护人权和民主，其成员数量比欧盟还多，但不要与欧洲理事会混淆。乌克兰是其成员国。 该组织秘书长阿兰·贝尔塞特表示：“俄罗斯为其侵略行为承担责任的时间很快就要到了。” “特别法庭代表正义和希望。现在需要采取行动，通过确保法庭的运作和资金来落实这一政治承诺。” 贝尔塞特说：“今天，我们正在承担责任，确保侵略不会得不到回应。”他邀请其他国家加入这一倡议。 乌克兰外交部长安德里·西比哈是周五的参与者之一，他称这次活动是“历史性的一天”。 “就像 80 年前的纽伦堡法庭一样，海牙特别法庭将从战争废墟中恢复正义，”西比哈说，他提到了二战后一些幸存的纳粹高级分子的审判。 “我们正在建立一个由三个支柱组成的问责基础设施：特别法庭、损失登记册和索赔委员会。我还要强调，问责制永远不会妥协。” 荷兰外交部长汤姆·贝伦德森表示，荷兰已同意在海牙“主持”特别法庭的“初始阶段”，海牙是其他几个国际法律机构和程序的所在地，其中最著名的是国际刑事法院。 贝伦德森说：“乌克兰的正义之路漫长且不易，但这并不能阻止我们竭尽全力帮助实现这一目标。” 批评者质疑，鉴于弗拉基米尔·普京总统的政权似乎不太可能合作或同意其制裁，这样一个法庭将如何能够起诉被指控的俄罗​​斯战犯或国家本身。 俄罗斯曾是欧洲委员会成员，但在...

title.en: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
title.zh: 巴基斯坦因在伊朗战争中发挥调解作用而面临压力

summary.en: With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.

Pakistan has taken on a leading role in the peace efforts between the US and Iran , hosting talks and serving as an intermediary for backchannel diplomacy between the warring parties .

For Islamabad, the stakes are high. Officials view stability in the Gulf as closely tied to the country's own economic and security interests. A broader confrontation between the US and Iran could disrupt trade routes, deepen energy pressures, inflame sectarian tensions and further destabilize Pakistan's sensitive border regions with Iran.

International prestige is also at play for the Pakistani government as they work to end a conflict affecting the entire world . But this also means a risk of reputational damage.

"Pakistan risks growing criticism if its efforts to revive US-Iran talks fail, especially after publicly taking a leading mediation role," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW. 

"With talks stalled, Pakistan's options are limited because a mediator cannot force two deeply distrustful sides to negotiate," he added.

"Pakistan is trying its best to engage both parties and views the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran with grave concern," a senior government official involved in the negotiation process told DW. 

"We are committed to playing a constructive diplomatic role to support immediate de-escalation and a peaceful resolution in the interest of regional and global security," the official added. 

Earlier this week, a report in US media raised doubt over Pakistan's neutrality in the Iran conflict. Citing unnamed US officials, CBS News reported that Pakistan had allowed Iran to park its aircraft on Pakistani airbases , effectively shielding them from US strikes.

Pakistan's Foreign Office immediately responded by calling the report "misleading" and "speculative." In an official statement, Islamabad said the aircraft activity was linked to diplomatic and logistical arrangements connected to ongoing peace efforts and involved personnel from multiple sides.

The Foreign Office also warned that "unverified and sensationalized reporting" risked undermining sensitive diplomatic initiatives.

US Senator Lindsey Graham, an outspoken supporter of the US war in Iran, publicly criticized Pakistan following the CBS report. His remarks reflect broader concerns among some US policymakers who fear Pakistan may be appearing too accommodating toward Tehran while still seeking to preserve strategic ties with Washington.

title.en: UK politics: How Starmer survives as Farage waits in wings
title.zh: 英国政治：斯塔默如何生存，法拉奇伺机而动

summary.en: The UK political landscape is marked by significant upheaval, including high-profile resignations, a prime minister facing pressure, and the increasing prominence of populist figures. This dynamic environment highlights the ongoing shifts within the Labour party and the rise of Nigel Farage.
summary.zh: 英国政坛正经历剧烈动荡，包括多位知名人士辞职、首相面临压力以及民粹主义者崛起。这种动态环境凸显了工党内部的持续变动以及奈杰尔·法拉奇的声势渐涨。

body.en:
High profile resignations, a prime minister on the edge and populists on the up — UK politics is far from dull. DW explains what's going on in Keir Starmer's Labour party and with Nigel Farage. And what may be next.

Less than two years after winning a landslide election victory that ended 14 years of center-right Conservative party governments in the UK, Keir Starmer is hanging by a thread.

His center-left Labour party lost well over half of their local council seats in elections held across England last week, with most going to right-wing, anti-immigration party, Reform UK. Labour also performed poorly in devolved elections for the Scottish and Welsh parliaments on the same day.

Because they operate at the national level, Starmer and his fellow Members of Parliament (MPs) weren't actually up for re-election. But the loss is perceived as a damning indictment of his lack of popularity. A survey this month by British pollsters YouGov found 23% of Britons held a positive opinion of Starmer, while 69% had an unfavorable view. He is also rapidly losing support within his party.

For now, the 63-year-old is still leading the country . Starmer's 2024 win means he is entitled to hold power until the next general election, which must be called by August 2029 at the latest. Unless he resigns, which he has so far ruled out , there are limited options to oust him during a term.

One of these is if he loses a so-called Parliamentary Vote of No Confidence. This must be tabled by an MP and Starmer must lose a simple majority in the House of Commons. Given Labour hold 403 of the 650 seats, this is unlikely. A more likely scenario is that he loses the support of his party.

More than 90 Labour MPs have called for him to go in recent days, with some high profile cabinet ministers resigning their posts. But, under Labour rules, 20% of Labour MPs — 81 people — must support a single candidate to challenge the incumbent. That scenario would trigger an internal party leadership election, the winner of which would become prime minister by default.

The early favorite isn't currently an MP. Andy Burnham is the elected Labour Mayor of Greater Manchester, one of the UK's largest cities and a traditional Labour heartland. That would ordinarily rule him out of a leadership challenge but Josh Simons, MP for Makerfield in Greater Manchester, has stepped down, forcing a byelection that Burnham hopes to win if selected by the party as candidate, giving him a seat in the House of Commons.

While Burnham has been well regarded in his mayoral stint, some will see his abandoning of Manchester for the big stage as a dereliction of duty. If he does win the byelection, Burnham will return to the national stage for the first time since 2017 having served under Tony Blair's government...
body.zh: 高调辞职、首相处于边缘、民粹主义者抬头——英国政治绝非沉闷。德国之声解释了凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 领导的工党和奈杰尔·法拉奇 (Nigel Farage) 的情况。接下来可能会发生什么。 凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 在选举中取得压倒性胜利，结束了英国 14 年的中右翼保守党政府统治，不到两年，他就命悬一线。 他的中左翼工党在上周英格兰各地举行的选举中失去了超过一半的地方议会席位，其中大部分席位被右翼反移民党改革英国所夺走。工党在同一天的苏格兰和威尔士议会权力下放选举中也表现不佳。 由于斯塔默和他的国会议员同僚是在国家层面运作的，因此他们实际上并没有竞选连任。但这次失利被认为是对他缺乏人气的严厉控诉。英国民意调查机构 YouGov 本月进行的一项调查发现，23% 的英国人对斯塔默持积极态度，而 69% 的人持负面看法。他也在党内迅速失去支持。 目前，这位63岁的老人仍然处于全国领先地位。斯塔默在 2024 年获胜意味着他有权在下一次大选之前继续掌权，而下一次大选最迟必须在 2029 年 8 月之前举行。除非他辞职（到目前为止他已经排除了这种可能性），否则在任期内罢免他的选择有限。 其中之一是如果他失去所谓的议会不信任投票。该提案必须由国会议员提出，而斯塔默必须在下议院失去简单多数。鉴于工党占据 650 个席位中的 403 个，这不太可能。更有可能的情况是他失去政党的支持。 最近几天，超过 90 名工党议员呼吁他下台，一些知名内阁部长也辞职了。但是，根据工党规定，20% 的工党议员（81 人）必须支持一名候选人才能挑战现任议员。这种情况将引发党内领导人选举，选举的获胜者将默认成为总理。 早期的热门人选目前不是国会议员。安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 是大曼彻斯特当选的工党市长，大曼彻斯特是英国最大的城市之一，也是传统的工党中心地带。这通常会使他排除在领导层挑战之外，但大曼彻斯特梅克菲尔德议员乔什·西蒙斯(Josh Simons)已经辞职，迫使伯纳姆进行补选，如果伯纳姆被该党选为候选人，他希望能够赢得补选，从而获得下议院席位。 尽管伯纳姆在市长任期内受到了良好的评价，但有些人会认为他放弃曼彻斯特而转向大舞台是一种失职。如果伯纳姆确实赢得补选，他将自 2017 年在托尼·布莱尔政府任职以来首次重返国家舞台……

As Donald Trump heaped praise on Xi Jinping during a meeting in Beijing, it was not reciprocated by the Chinese president. Instead, Xi invoked an ancient Greek concept, signalling there could be trouble ahead.

The United States president is on a three-day state visit to China — the first by an American president since his own in 2017 — where he's hoping to secure assistance from the Iranian ally over opening the Strait of Hormuz, among other objectives.

On Thursday, before their two-hour private meeting at the Great Hall of the People, Trump lavished praise on Xi, saying he is a "great leader" and that "it's an honour to be your friend".

Xi, on the other hand, implied that the US was on the way out as global hegemon while China was quickly taking its place, with a subtle warning that its rivals ought not to stop its ascendance.

"Currently, a transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, and the international situation is fluid and turbulent," he said.

"The world has come to a new crossroads. Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations?"

That concept, referencing the Greek historian's assessment of the second Peloponnesian War of 431 BC to 404 BC, posits that a rising power strikes fear into a regional leader, making war inevitable.

According to Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning, Xi told Trump that "the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations".

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy," Xi is alleged to have said.

Such militaristic posturing is nothing new from China, according to Bethany Allen, head of China investigations and analysis at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI).

"It's all very, very similar language to what we've seen before," she told SBS News. "China is always firm on Taiwan."

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state who is with Trump in Beijing, has said that such remarks are routine for China.

“They always raise it on their side," he told NBC News. "We always make clear our position, and we move on to the other topics.”

The conflict in the Middle East has seen US allies — including Australia — refuse to respond to requests for assistance in opening the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway's closure has driven up fuel costs around the world and impacted Trump's approval ratings domestically in the US.

body.en:
On the eve of the Eurovision grand final, Delta Goodrem has deflected questions about boycotts over Israel’s participation, saying her role is to believe in the "healing power" of music — not politics.

Goodrem progressed to the song contest’s grand final after impressing judges during Friday morning’s semi-final performance for her song, Eclipse.

In an interview with SBS before her semi-final performance, Goodrem addressed the boycott of this year's contest, the pressure to represent Australia, and called for Australia to host the song contest should she win.

This year’s contest is smaller than usual, with Iceland, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Spain — the latter of which typically has a guaranteed place in the grand final as one of the contest's largest financial contributors — all withdrawing in protest at Israel’s continued inclusion amid the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

An assault by Hamas on 7 October 2023 killed 1,200 people, according to Israeli tallies. More than 72,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israel's retaliatory action in Gaza since, according to local health authorities.

Asked directly about the boycott, Goodrem declined to take a position, instead pointing to her long-held belief in music as a unifying force.

"When you come to my shows, I tell you to leave everything outside the door — come in here and we're singing the same song," she said before her semi-final performance.

"From the day I got into music, I have always believed in the power of music and its healing qualities.

"That's really my focus and that's really what I have wholeheartedly believed in from day one — that's kind of where I stay true on my north star."

SBS — an associate member of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and Australia's official Eurovision broadcaster — has continued its participation in and coverage of the contest this year, arguing that withdrawing would compromise its editorial independence and impartiality.

"SBS recognises and respects the deeply held views and concerns about the war in the Middle East and its impact," an SBS spokesperson previously said.

"Our responsibility is to provide comprehensive, trusted and impartial coverage for Australians across our network, and we will continue to do so."

The Eurovision Song Contest maintains that it is "strictly non-political" and not intended to be used as a platform for "political expression, activism, controversy or the promotion of external causes or agendas".

Russia was excluded from the contest after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title.zh: 达美·古德雷姆 (Delta Goodrem) 带领澳大利亚进入欧洲歌唱大赛决赛

summary.en: Australia progresses through the semi-finals at the 70th Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna, Austria.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Delta Goodrem has taken Australia to the Eurovision song contest finals for the first time in three years.

The Australian singer-songwriter delivered a spectacular semi-final performance on Friday morning of her song Eclipse at the Wiener Stadthalle in Vienna, Austria.

The country was voted through to the finals by popular vote, which will take place on Saturday night local time (Sunday morning AEST).

Australia joins Bulgaria, Ukraine, Norway, Romania, Malta, Cyprus, Albania, Denmark, and Czechia in the finals.

Those second-round winners will compete against first-round winners: Greece, Finland, Belgium, Sweden, Moldova, Israel, Serbia, Croatia, Lithuania, and Poland.

There have been 95,000 tickets sold for this year's event to fans from 75 countries and territories, and the European Broadcasting Union expects it will be the largest live audience in years.

Goodrem spoke to SBS News' chief international correspondent Ben Lewis on Thursday ahead of her performance, telling him that she was "excited" to take her song to the Austrian stage and that Eurovision is a world of its own.

"It's really special, it's a really incredible way to step into the music where people can get to know the songs and support the songs ... It's really amazing to learn all the different aspects of this," Goodrem said.

The singer's pop power ballad is an original track written by Goodrem in collaboration with Grammy-winning Swedish songwriter Jonas Myrin and Los Angeles-based songwriter Ferras Alqaisi.

Performing on a raised platform, Goodrem joked that the stage theatrics took her "a bit higher than I realised".

She added that she felt her fellow Australian icon and Eurovision predecessor, Olivia Newton-John, would be "watching over" the proceedings.

On the idea that she might deliver Australia its first-ever Eurovision victory, Goodrem argued the country would make an "amazing" host and that Europeans would simply have to get up at 4am — as Australians are accustomed to doing each year.

The winner of Eurovision's country of origin will traditionally host the event the following year.

The second semi-final will be broadcast in Australia at 5am AEST on Friday 15 May.

SBS will also broadcast the grand final live at 5am AEST on Sunday 17 May, with the SBS News online team covering all the action in a live blog.

For those who want a sleep-in — or to relive the excitement — SBS will air prime-time 'access all areas' broadcasts from 15–17 May at 7.30pm AEST.

For the latest from SBS News,  download our app and  subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 黛尔塔·古德雷姆 (Delta Goodrem) 三年来首次带领澳大利亚进入欧洲歌唱大赛决赛。 这位澳大利亚歌手兼作曲家于周五上午在奥地利维也纳的维也纳体育场进行了一场精彩的半决赛表演，演唱了她的歌曲《Eclipse》。 该国通过全民投票进入决赛，决赛将于当地时间周六晚上（澳大利亚东部标准时间周日上午）举行。 澳大利亚队与保加利​​亚队、乌克兰队、挪威队、罗马尼亚队、马耳他队、塞浦路斯队、阿尔巴尼亚队、丹麦队和捷克队一起进入决赛。 第二轮获胜者将与第一轮获胜者竞争：希腊、芬兰、比利时、瑞典、摩尔多瓦、以色列、塞尔维亚、克罗地亚、立陶宛和波兰。 今年的赛事已向来自 75 个国家和地区的球迷售出了 95,000 张门票，欧洲广播联盟预计这将是多年来现场观众人数最多的一次。 周四，古德雷姆在演出前接受了 SBS 新闻首席国际记者本·路易斯 (Ben Lewis) 的采访，她告诉他，她很“兴奋”将自己的歌曲带到奥地利舞台，而且欧洲歌唱大赛是一个独立的世界。 “这真的很特别，这是一种真正令人难以置信的进入音乐的方式，人们可以了解这些歌曲并支持这些歌曲......了解这一切的不同方面真是太神奇了，”古德雷姆说。 这位歌手的流行力量民谣是古德雷姆与格莱美获奖者瑞典歌曲作家乔纳斯·迈林和洛杉矶歌曲作家费拉斯·阿尔盖西合作创作的原创歌曲。 在升高的平台上表演时，古德莱姆开玩笑说，舞台表演让她“比我意识到的要高一些”。 她补充说，她觉得她的澳大利亚偶像、欧洲电视网前任奥利维亚·牛顿-约翰将“监督”整个过程。 关于她可能为澳大利亚带来有史以来第一次欧洲歌唱大赛胜利的想法，古德雷姆认为，这个国家将成为一个“令人惊叹的”东道主，欧洲人只需要凌晨 4 点起床——就像澳大利亚人每年习惯的那样。 按照惯例，欧洲歌唱大赛原籍国的获胜者将主办次年的赛事。 第二场半决赛将于 5 月 15 日星期五上午 5 点（澳大利亚东部标准时间）在澳大利亚播出。 SBS 还将在 5 月 17 日（星期日）澳大利亚东部标准时间早上 5 点直播总决赛，SBS 新闻在线团队将在直播博客中报道所有活动。 对于那些想要睡个懒觉或者重温兴奋感的人来说，SBS 将于 5 月 15 日至 17 日澳大利亚东部标准时间晚上 7 点 30 分播出黄金时段“访问所有区域”广播。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: Trump warns Taiwan against declaring independence, hours after summit with China's Xi
title.zh: 与中国习近平峰会数小时后，特朗普警告台湾不要宣布独立

summary.en: The US president says he wants Beijing and Taipei to "cool down" tensions over the self-governing island.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump has cautioned Taiwan against formally declaring independence from China.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent," the US president told Fox News on Friday, at the end of his two-day summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Trump earlier said he had "made no commitment either way" about the self-governing island - which China claims as part of its territory and has not ruled out taking by force.

The US has long supported Taiwan, including being bound by law to provide it with a means of self-defence, but has frequently had to square this alliance with maintaining a diplomatic relationship with China.

Washington's established position is that it does not support Taiwanese independence, with continued ties with Beijing being contingent on its acceptance that there is only one Chinese government.

Many Taiwanese consider themselves to be part of a separate nation - though most are in favour of maintaining the status quo in which Taiwan neither declares independence from China nor unites with it.

In his interview with Fox News, Trump reiterated that US policy on the matter had not changed.

"You know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles (15,289km) to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down."

On the flight back to Washington, the US president had told reporters that he and Xi had spoken "a lot" about the island, but said he had declined to discuss whether the US would defend it.

Xi "feels very strongly" about the island and "doesn't want to see a movement for independence", Trump said.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations," Xi warned during the talks, according to Chinese state media, adding: "If mishandled, the two nations could collide or even come into conflict."

Asked if he foresaw a conflict with China over Taiwan, Trump had said: "No, I don't think so. I think we'll be fine. [Xi] doesn't want to see a war."

China has ramped up military drills around the island in recent years, raising tensions in the region and testing the balance that Washington has struck.

Late last year, the Trump administration announced an $11bn ($8bn) package of weapons to be sold to Taiwan , including advanced rocket launchers and a variety of missiles, which Beijing condemned.

Trump said he would soon decide whether that sale could go ahead, adding that he and Xi had discussed it "in great detail" and that he would speak to Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te first.

"We're not looking to have wars, and if you kept it the way it is, I think China's going to be OK with that. But we're not looking to have somebody say, 'Let's go independent because the United States is backing us'."

body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普警告台湾不要正式宣布从中国独立。 “我不希望有人独立，”美国总统周五在北京与中国国家主席习近平为期两天的峰会结束时告诉福克斯新闻。 特朗普早些时候表示，他对这个自治岛屿“没有做出任何承诺”——中国声称该岛是其领土的一部分，并且不排除以武力夺取该岛的可能性。 美国长期以来一直支持台湾，包括受法律约束为其提供自卫手段，但经常不得不将这一联盟与维持与中国的外交关系结合起来。 华盛顿的既定立场是，它不支持台湾独立，与北京继续保持关系取决于它是否接受只有一个中国政府。 许多台湾人认为自己是一个独立国家的一部分，尽管大多数人赞成维持现状，即台湾既不宣布从中国独立，也不与中国统一。 特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时重申，美国在此事上的政策没有改变。 “你知道，我们应该行驶 9,500 英里（15,289 公里）去打一场战争。我不是在寻找那个。我希望他们冷静下来。我希望中国冷静下来。” 在返回华盛顿的航班上，美国总统告诉记者，他和习近平就该岛“谈了很多”，但表示他拒绝讨论美国是否会保卫该岛。 特朗普表示，习近平对该岛“感情非常强烈”，并且“不希望看到独立运动”。 据中国官方媒体报道，习近平在会谈中警告称，“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题”，并补充说：“如果处理不当，两国可能发生冲突甚至冲突。” 当被问及是否预见到与中国在台湾问题上发生冲突时，特朗普表示：“不，我不这么认为。我认为我们会没事的。[习近平]不想看到战争。” 近年来，中国加大了在该岛周围的军事演习力度，加剧了该地区的紧张局势，并考验着华盛顿所达成的平衡。 去年年底，特朗普政府宣布向台湾出售价值 110 亿美元（约合 80 亿美元）的一揽子武器，其中包括先进火箭发射器和各种导弹，北京对此予以谴责。 特朗普表示，他将很快决定是否继续进行这项出售，并补充说，他和习近平已经“非常详细”地讨论了此事，他将首先与台湾总统赖清德通话。 “我们不希望发生战争，如果保持现状，我认为中国会对此表示同意。但我们不希望有人说，‘让我们独立吧，因为美国支持我们’。” 此前，美国因看似...而激怒了中国。

title.en: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
title.zh: 巴基斯坦在伊朗战争调解中面临压力

summary.en: Pakistan is navigating a complex geopolitical landscape as it attempts to mediate in a major conflict involving Iran, balancing relationships with Washington, Tehran, Beijing, and key Gulf allies. Recent media scrutiny has intensified the pressure on Islamabad.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦正努力调解一场涉及伊朗的重大地缘政治冲突，同时需平衡与华盛顿、德黑兰、北京以及主要海湾盟友的关系，这使其面临复杂的局面。近期一份美国媒体报道进一步加剧了伊斯兰堡所承受的压力。

body.en:
With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.

Pakistan has taken on a leading role in the peace efforts between the US and Iran , hosting talks and serving as an intermediary for backchannel diplomacy between the warring parties .

For Islamabad, the stakes are high. Officials view stability in the Gulf as closely tied to the country's own economic and security interests. A broader confrontation between the US and Iran could disrupt trade routes, deepen energy pressures, inflame sectarian tensions and further destabilize Pakistan's sensitive border regions with Iran.

International prestige is also at play for the Pakistani government as they work to end a conflict affecting the entire world . But this also means a risk of reputational damage.

"Pakistan risks growing criticism if its efforts to revive US-Iran talks fail, especially after publicly taking a leading mediation role," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW. 

"With talks stalled, Pakistan's options are limited because a mediator cannot force two deeply distrustful sides to negotiate," he added.

"Pakistan is trying its best to engage both parties and views the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran with grave concern," a senior government official involved in the negotiation process told DW. 

"We are committed to playing a constructive diplomatic role to support immediate de-escalation and a peaceful resolution in the interest of regional and global security," the official added. 

Earlier this week, a report in US media raised doubt over Pakistan's neutrality in the Iran conflict. Citing unnamed US officials, CBS News reported that Pakistan had allowed Iran to park its aircraft on Pakistani airbases , effectively shielding them from US strikes.

Pakistan's Foreign Office immediately responded by calling the report "misleading" and "speculative." In an official statement, Islamabad said the aircraft activity was linked to diplomatic and logistical arrangements connected to ongoing peace efforts and involved personnel from multiple sides.

The Foreign Office also warned that "unverified and sensationalized reporting" risked undermining sensitive diplomatic initiatives.

US Senator Lindsey Graham, an outspoken supporter of the US war in Iran, publicly criticized Pakistan following the CBS report. His remarks reflect broader concerns among some US policymakers who fear Pakistan may be appearing too accommodating toward Tehran while still seeking to preserve strategic ties with Washington.

title.en: Seth Meyers on Trump sucking up to Xi: ‘What happened to standing up to China?’
title.zh: 赛斯·梅耶斯谈特朗普对习近平的奉承：‘说好的对抗中国呢？’

summary.en: Late-night television hosts commented on the US president's recent trip to China, where his seemingly deferential remarks towards President Xi Jinping, including calling it an “honor” to be his friend, drew criticism for appearing inconsistent with previous rhetoric about standing up to China.
summary.zh: 深夜脱口秀主持人评论了美国总统最近的中国之行，期间总统对习近平主席表现出的恭维言论，包括称与习主席为友是“荣幸”，引发了对其此前“对抗中国”言论不一致的批评。

body.en:
Late-night hosts discussed Donald Trump ’s trip to China and his mixed reception.

On Late Night, Seth Meyers noted that in Trump‘s first year of his second term his family made about $4bn , an “insane” figure that was “not even from doing anything” other than government contracts, shady crypto deals and memecoins.

Recently, a 91-storey Trump tower on Australia’s Gold Coast was scrapped after it was decided that the Trump brand is “increasingly toxic” in the country.

He said as he is loathed overseas, it’s a “perfect time for the president to fly to China” before playing footage of his welcome, which included a group of children dancing and cheering.

Trump remarked on how beautiful the children were and, in character, Meyers joked: “The last time I saw so many young and beautiful children greet a plane, it was on an island.”

He has also been joined by his son Eric, to which Meyers said: “Just imagine the rightwing freakout if Hunter Biden had gone with Joe on a trip to China.”

Trump also arrived with an “entourage of American CEOs” including Elon Musk who Meyers said would need to “project dignity and poise” something he failed at instantly with footage of him acting strangely at a party then played.

“The fuck are you doing, dude?” Meyers asked, saying he looked “like an eight-year-old who’s ruining the family Christmas card”.

Trump was aiming to stand up to Xi Jinping after years of calling out China for how the US has been treated yet the president said many fawning comments including how it was an “honor” to be the leader’s friend.

His arrival was mocked across China online and state censors have been allowing comments to go viral.

“Internet memes and posts are hardly behind Trump’s back. They’re mocking him where he’s most likely to see it ,” he said.

Meyers said, as Americans struggle to get by, all Trump cares about it “flattery, fanfare and self-enrichment” overseas.

On the Late Show, Stephen Colbert also spoke about Trump’s trip to Beijing , joking about Trump and Xi’s “inspiring display of hyper-masculine hand dominance” as they shared an extended awkward handshake.

Colbert warned that Xi “might catch a case of five-day-old banana hand” if he isn’t careful.

He also played footage of the welcoming committee of excited children, saying: “Those kids are so happy … that they got the day off from the iPhone factory.”

The visit also saw Trump say how much he respected the Chinese leader, adding that he only says the truth. Colbert joked that it was his “one billionth lie”.

While many members of the press were there to cover, a CBS journalist failed to get a visa in time and had to cover from Taiwan instead.

Colbert said that it fits into the CBS slogan: “When events happen, we’re at most one country away.”

summary.en: Donald Trump hopes to have China help him end the war in Iran, but this goal seemed far from guaranteed as he wrapped up his two-day visit to Beijing. Xi Jinping, in turn, took the chance to warn the US over Taiwan.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Donald Trump hopes to have China help him end the war in Iran, but this goal seemed far from guaranteed as he wrapped up his two-day visit to Beijing. Xi Jinping, in turn, took the chance to warn the US over Taiwan.

The high-profile Beijing summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping ended with bombastic, positive statements — especially from the Trump White House, which called the US president "the dealmaker-in-chief" — but with little info known about concrete deals between the two rival superpowers.

Trump praised Xi during the visit, calling him a "great leader" and "a man I respect greatly."

Addressing reporters at a press event alongside Xi, Trump also indicated that he and Xi "feel very similar" about the Iran war, which has been dominating global politics since the US and Israel launched air strikes on Iran in late February .

"We want that to end. We don't want them to have a nuclear weapon. We want the straits open," Trump said.  

This echoed Trump's previous claims of Xi offering to help broker a deal with Tehran and open the Strait of Hormuz .

The Chinese leader, however, did not mention Iran in his remarks to the press on Friday. Instead, Xi took the chance to warn of a potential conflict between China and the US if the two nations fail to cooperate. He highlighted the dispute over Taiwan , the self-ruled island which China sees as its own territory.

"The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,"  Xi said.

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy."

With global economy in turmoil over the Strait of Hormuz, neither side seems willing to return to the bruising trade war of 2025 .

The US president was accompanied by more than a dozen CEOs, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Apple's Tim Cook and Tesla's Elon Musk .

On Friday, Trump touted "fantastic trade deals for both countries," without providing details.

Joseph Bosco, a former China Country Desk Officer in the US Office of the Secretary of Defense, told DW that Xi was trying to "exploit Trump's obvious vulnerabilities at this point."

Trump "has the Iran war going on, which is not going according to his original plan. And I think Xi Jinping thought this is a good time to press very hard on the most important issue that they perceive, which is Taiwan," Bosco said.

The United States president is on a three-day state visit to China — the first by an American president since his own in 2017 — where he's hoping to secure assistance from the Iranian ally over opening the Strait of Hormuz, among other objectives.

On Thursday, before their two-hour private meeting at the Great Hall of the People, Trump lavished praise on Xi, saying he is a "great leader" and that "it's an honour to be your friend".

Xi, on the other hand, implied that the US was on the way out as global hegemon while China was quickly taking its place, with a subtle warning that its rivals ought not to stop its ascendance.

"Currently, a transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, and the international situation is fluid and turbulent," he said.

"The world has come to a new crossroads. Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations?"

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy," Xi is alleged to have said.

"It's all very, very similar language to what we've seen before," she told SBS News. "China is always firm on Taiwan."

“They always raise it on their side," he told NBC News. "We always make clear our position, and we move on to the other topics.”

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is headed home to Washington after spending two days with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing. Both leaders struck a cordial tone, but no concrete agreements were announced. Follow DW.

Donald Trump hopes to have China help him end the war in Iran, but this goal seemed far from guaranteed as he wrapped up his two-day visit to Beijing. Xi Jinping, in turn, took the chance to warn the US over Taiwan.

The high-profile Beijing summit  between  Donald Trump  and  Xi Jinping  ended with bombastic, positive statements — especially from the Trump White House, which called the US president "the dealmaker-in-chief" — but with little info known about concrete deals between the two rival superpowers.

US President Donald Trump in an interview with Fox News aired after meeting China's Xi Jinping said that there was nothing for Taiwan to worry about on the US position towards the self-ruled island, but added he "doesn't want somebody go independent and we're supposed to go travel 9,500 miles to fight a war."

Under the Taiwan Relations Act the US is bound to provide defensive weaponry to Taiwan, but is not bound by treaty to use military force to defend the island. 

In December, a massive $11 billion weapons package for Taiwan was approved by Trump's administration, as was another $14 billion arms sale in January. However, Trump must approve both packages for them to move forwards. 

Asked about approving the billions of dollars in US weapons sales , Trump said "we're going to see what happens … I may do it , I may not do it."

On Friday, Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said it had taken note of Trump's statements, and thanked the president for having approved previous arms sales. 

"Regarding Taiwan-U.S. arms sales, they are not only a security commitment to Taiwan explicitly set out by the United States in the Taiwan Relations ⁠Act, but also ​a form of joint deterrence against regional threats," Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

US President Donald Trump on Friday warned Taiwan against seeking independence and relying on US support, suggesting he had no interest in joining a war triggered by such a move.

"We're not looking to have wars, and if you kept it the way it is, I think China's going to be OK with that," Trump told Fox News' Bret Baier in an interview. "But we're not looking at somebody saying, 'let's go independent because the United States is backing us.'"

The statements follow a high stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who on Thursday warned the US that relations with China hinge upon the question of Taiwan and the extent of US support to the self-ruled island.

Hopefully, an impending rise to the minimum wage will help low-income earners, although the debate on how much to actually lift it stepped up this week.

And as the market awaits official jobs numbers next week, we took a look at how AI is shaping the hiring market.

The federal budget delivered one of the biggest shake-ups to property investment tax settings in years.

Negative gearing will be limited to newly-built homes , while the current 50 per cent capital gains tax discount will be replaced by a model linked to inflation.

Future investment gains will also face a minimum 30 per cent tax rate, although most existing investments will receive some grandfathering protections .

Bank shares tumbled with CBA suffering its worst one-day decline on record during the week.

There are fears the new rules may hit the investor loan books of banks across the board, but it also came as CBA unveiled its quarterly profit result and warned of a tougher economic climate ahead.

As its share price fell, BHP rose to its highest on record to overtake the bank as Australia’s largest listed company.

The debate over wages intensified this week after unions lifted their push for a six per cent increase to the minimum wage from five per cent.

The revised move came after the federal budget forecast inflation would peak at five per cent by the middle of this year before easing to around 2.5 per cent next year.

If granted, the increase would lift the minimum wage to $26.45 an hour, or just over $1,000 a week.

But employer groups are pushing back hard. The Australian Industry Group labelled the proposal “ludicrous”, arguing anything above its proposed 3.9 per cent increase could worsen inflation and damage businesses already facing rising costs and weaker economic conditions.

New research by recruiters Michael Page shows two-thirds of white-collar workers are now using AI tools to help write resumes, tailor job applications and improve wording.

Employers are also embracing the technology, with many using AI to draft job descriptions and interview questions.

For job seekers, AI can help sharpen applications and save time. But recruiters warn there is a risk of overusing it, especially if applications become too generic or inaccurate.

The shift also highlights how quickly AI is becoming embedded in everyday work and career decisions well beyond the technology sector.

title.en: A secretive way to preserve wealth in Australia is finally facing a crackdown
title.zh: 澳大利亚一种秘密的财富保值方式终于面临打击

summary.en: Some Australians have benefited for decades from a secretive arrangement that allows them to hide assets and reduce tax.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

Australians know almost nothing about the one million trusts in the country except for the details that have emerged via messy family legal disputes over million-dollar assets.

Even the beneficiaries of these trusts can be left in the dark about their operations and don't always get the money that is distributed to them 'on paper'.

The details of trusts — particularly discretionary trusts — are shrouded in secrecy, and power lies with the trustee who manages the assets.

But the popularity of trusts in Australia has skyrocketed. They have doubled in number in less than 20 years, from 501,860 in 2003/04 to more than one million in 2022/23.

For decades, groups like the Australian Council of Social Service (ACOSS) have been calling for more transparency around trusts, which have been used for money laundering and to hide assets in family court matters.

Australia does not have a public registry that provides details about trusts, and the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) doesn't maintain a register of trust deeds with beneficiaries' details.

ACOSS says trusts have also been "used and abused by well-off taxpayers for many years" for tax minimisation.

"It beggars belief that so many people use these for any other reason than to avoid tax," ACOSS CEO Cassandra Goldie says.

Employees who receive a salary or wage generally can't direct their income into trusts because of rules that prevent them from avoiding tax.

They are generally used only by those who own businesses or have income-producing assets, such as rental properties or share portfolios.

According to data from 2019-20, the wealthiest 10 per cent of households hold more than 90 per cent of private trust wealth.

The government is now cracking down on trusts, announcing changes in this year's budget on how they will be taxed.

The debate has renewed scrutiny on how trusts operate, and why a system controlling vast amounts of wealth remains largely hidden from public view.

At their core, a trust consists of one person — the trustee — who holds the legal title to its assets but must manage these for the benefit of others — the beneficiaries.

There are many types of trusts. One common example is a "fixed trust", which allows people to invest money in a project, and to receive a fixed percentage of income. Before modern corporations became widespread, these trusts were often used as an early form of collective investment structure.

Trusts developed in medieval England and were often used as a way for people to provide for widows and children. Today, they are used for a much broader range of purposes, including estate planning, charitable giving, business...

title.en: The 'Thucydides trap' and Taiwan: What the US' visit to China means for Australia
title.zh: “修昔底德陷阱”与台湾：美国访华对澳大利亚意味着什么

summary.en: Xi Jinping has demonstrated his resolve in front of a diminished Donald Trump.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Donald Trump heaped praise on Xi Jinping during a meeting in Beijing, it was not reciprocated by the Chinese president. Instead, Xi invoked an ancient Greek concept, signalling there could be trouble ahead.

The United States president is on a three-day state visit to China — the first by an American president since his own in 2017 — where he's hoping to secure assistance from the Iranian ally over opening the Strait of Hormuz, among other objectives.

On Thursday, before their two-hour private meeting at the Great Hall of the People, Trump lavished praise on Xi, saying he is a "great leader" and that "it's an honour to be your friend".

Xi, on the other hand, implied that the US was on the way out as global hegemon while China was quickly taking its place, with a subtle warning that its rivals ought not to stop its ascendance.

"Currently, a transformation not seen in a century is accelerating across the globe, and the international situation is fluid and turbulent," he said.

"The world has come to a new crossroads. Can China and the United States overcome the Thucydides trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations?"

That concept, referencing the Greek historian's assessment of the second Peloponnesian War of 431 BC to 404 BC, posits that a rising power strikes fear into a regional leader, making war inevitable.

According to Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning, Xi told Trump that "the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations".

"If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy," Xi is alleged to have said.

Such militaristic posturing is nothing new from China, according to Bethany Allen, head of China investigations and analysis at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute (ASPI).

"It's all very, very similar language to what we've seen before," she told SBS News. "China is always firm on Taiwan."

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state who is with Trump in Beijing, has said that such remarks are routine for China.

“They always raise it on their side," he told NBC News. "We always make clear our position, and we move on to the other topics.”

The conflict in the Middle East has seen US allies — including Australia — refuse to respond to requests for assistance in opening the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway's closure has driven up fuel costs around the world and impacted Trump's approval ratings domestically in the US.

"Trump is coming into this in a significantly weakened position, then I would say we have ever seen from the US before," she said.

title.en: Could Australia win Eurovision? The odds are looking Goodrem
title.zh: 澳大利亚能否赢得欧洲歌唱大赛？古德伦的胜算看好

summary.en: Delta Goodrem has progressed to the grand final of the Eurovision Song Contest, where she is one of the favourites to win.
summary.zh: 黛尔塔·古德伦已晋级欧洲歌唱大赛总决赛，她被视为夺冠热门之一。

body.en:
On the eve of the Eurovision grand final, Delta Goodrem has deflected questions about boycotts over Israel’s participation, saying her role is to believe in the "healing power" of music — not politics.

Goodrem progressed to the song contest’s grand final after impressing judges during Friday morning’s semi-final performance for her song, Eclipse.

In an interview with SBS before her semi-final performance, Goodrem addressed the boycott of this year's contest, the pressure to represent Australia, and called for Australia to host the song contest should she win.

This year’s contest is smaller than usual, with Iceland, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Spain — the latter of which typically has a guaranteed place in the grand final as one of the contest's largest financial contributors — all withdrawing in protest at Israel’s continued inclusion amid the ongoing conflict in Gaza.

An assault by Hamas on 7 October 2023 killed 1,200 people, according to Israeli tallies. More than 72,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israel's retaliatory action in Gaza since, according to local health authorities.

Asked directly about the boycott, Goodrem declined to take a position, instead pointing to her long-held belief in music as a unifying force.

"When you come to my shows, I tell you to leave everything outside the door — come in here and we're singing the same song," she said before her semi-final performance.

"From the day I got into music, I have always believed in the power of music and its healing qualities.

"That's really my focus and that's really what I have wholeheartedly believed in from day one — that's kind of where I stay true on my north star."

SBS — an associate member of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) and Australia's official Eurovision broadcaster — has continued its participation in and coverage of the contest this year, arguing that withdrawing would compromise its editorial independence and impartiality.

"SBS recognises and respects the deeply held views and concerns about the war in the Middle East and its impact," an SBS spokesperson previously said.

"Our responsibility is to provide comprehensive, trusted and impartial coverage for Australians across our network, and we will continue to do so."

The Eurovision Song Contest maintains that it is "strictly non-political" and not intended to be used as a platform for "political expression, activism, controversy or the promotion of external causes or agendas".

Russia was excluded from the contest after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

title.en: 'No place in Australia': Burke adds 'neo-Nazis' to proscribed hate group list
title.zh: “澳大利亚没有立足之地”：伯克将“新纳粹分子”添加到被禁止的仇恨团体名单中

summary.en: The home affairs minister has used powers established in the wake of the Bondi attack to prohibit a second hate group.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The federal government has banned a neo-Nazi group, formerly known as the National Socialist Network (NSN), adding it to the prohibited hate group list.

Under hate group laws introduced after the Bondi Beach terror attack , a new legal framework was established that allows the home affairs minister to ban groups found to be engaging in or advocating hate crimes based on race, nationality or ethnic origin.

The NSN, Australia's most prominent white supremacist group, announced in January this year that it was disbanding in its entirety in response to the legislation, along with its "co-projects" White Australia, the White Australia Party and the European Australian Movement.

On Friday, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said a strict process had taken place, initiated by the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation, with the initial threshold for further investigation met in late April.

"Today, the organisation that would be colloquially known as the neo-Nazis, but it's gone through different names — the European Australian movement, the National Socialist Network, and White Australia — has been listed as the second prohibited hate group under the changes that were made to the criminal code," he said.

He explained that supporting, funding, training, recruiting, joining or directing the group would be a criminal offence from midnight.

"None of this will stop bigoted people from having horrific ideologies, but it does prevent this group from organising, from meeting and prevents some of the sorts of horrific bigoted rallies that we have seen around our country," he said.

"It sends a clear message to people who believe in racial supremacy that their views have no place in Australia."

He noted that even if the organisation reforms under a new name, it will remain listed following a "simple regulation change".

Executive Council of Australian Jewry co-chief executive Peter Wertheim welcomed the announcement, saying it "will send a much-needed message that these groups and their hateful, racist ideology has no place in Australia".

“The ECAJ has been calling for this measure since 2021. We told a parliamentary committee at the time that groups like NSN were operating at a level just below the threshold required to list them as a terrorist organisation, but were using social media in the same way as terrorist groups to groom and recruit impressionable young men to join them.

"It doesn’t matter what they call themselves, or how they structure themselves, these groups use all the well-known techniques of thuggery and menace that Nazis have always used against Jewish communities and other groups they have targeted."

body.zh: 联邦政府禁止了一个新纳粹组织（原名国家社会主义网络（NSN）），并将其添加到被禁止的仇恨组织名单中。 根据邦迪海滩恐怖袭击后出台的仇恨团体法，建立了一个新的法律框架，允许内政部长禁止被发现从事或倡导基于种族、国籍或族裔的仇恨犯罪的团体。 澳大利亚最著名的白人至上主义组织 NSN 于今年 1 月宣布，为响应这项立法，该组织及其“合作项目”白澳大利亚、白澳大利亚党和欧洲澳大利亚运动将全部解散。 周五，内政部长托尼·伯克表示，澳大利亚安全情报组织发起了严格的程序，并于四月下旬达到了进一步调查的初步门槛。 他说：“今天，这个通俗地称为新纳粹的组织，但它已经有了不同的名字——欧洲澳大利亚运动、国家社会主义网络和白澳大利亚——根据刑法的修改，已被列为第二个被禁止的仇恨团体。” 他解释说，从午夜开始，支持、资助、培训、招募、加入或指挥该组织将构成刑事犯罪。 他说：“所有这些都无法阻止偏执的人拥有可怕的意识形态，但它确实阻止了这个团体的组织、聚会，并阻止了我们在我国各地看到的一些可怕的偏执集会。” “这向相信种族至上的人们发出了一个明确的信息，即他们的观点在澳大利亚没有立足之地。” 他指出，即使该组织以新名称进行改革，在“简单的监管变化”后，它仍将保持在名单上。 澳大利亚犹太人执行委员会联席首席执行官彼得·沃特海姆 (Peter Wertheim) 对这一消息表示欢迎，称这“将发出一个急需的信息，即这些群体及其仇恨的种族主义意识形态在澳大利亚没有立足之地”。 “ECAJ 自 2021 年以来一直呼吁采取这一措施。当时我们告诉议会委员会，像 NSN 这样的组织的运作水平略低于将其列为恐怖组织所需的门槛，但它们却像恐怖组织一样利用社交媒体来培养和招募易受影响的年轻人加入他们。 “无论他们如何称呼自己，或者如何组织自己，这些团体都使用所有众所周知的凶杀和威胁手段，纳粹一直对犹太社区和他们瞄准的其他群体使用这些手段。” 这是继禁止伊斯兰教之后第二次援引新的仇恨言论法……
